A1.justification: Both complete, readable 25-page PDFs describe the same MedTrinity-25M and LLaVA-Tri work. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching throughout, including Tables 1-6, Figures 1-14, and Appendices A-F.

before.justification: v2 reports original VQA experiments, alignment ablations, expert and LLM annotation evaluations, and a caption comparison in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies, including revised LLaVA-Tri results in Tables 3-4.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, retrieval and ROI components, LLaVA-Medcap generation procedure, and LLaVA-Tri architecture remain unchanged. The revised downstream training duration is an experimental-setting change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MedTrinity-25M sources and coverage, documented in Appendix A, and evaluate on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA. No datasets, tasks, populations, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains all nine comparators and their benchmark participation. Table 4 also retains the same model comparisons. Separating non-MLLM and MLLM rows changes presentation, not comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported fine-tuning budget from 3 to 15 epochs on each of the three VQA datasets, adding that this follows LLaVA-Med. This fivefold budget revision substantially changes the stated conditions of the central experiments; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the description was corrected.

E4.justification: Table 4 revises the evidence for the existing alignment ablation by replacing both aligned and unaligned LLaVA-Tri results. The ablation question, other model comparisons, qualitative component analyses, and appendix studies remain unchanged; no new ablation or robustness test is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The parenthesized additions in Table 4 remain performance gains, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported LLaVA-Tri averages change from 81.6/87.8/82.8 to 75.0/87.8/65.3 on VQA-RAD/SLAKE/PathVQA. Table 4's corresponding alignment gains change from 10.8/6.1/8.3 to 2.0/5.0/1.6 points. PathVQA open accuracy now ties LLaVA-Med at 37.9. Baseline component scores remain unchanged, while Table 3 removes average entries. These are substantial replacement results under a changed reported budget, not established same-setting performance declines.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added, removed, or revised. The methodological descriptions and appendices retain the same content.

C1.justification: The dataset and automated-pipeline contributions, broad applicability claims, and claim of state-of-the-art performance on all three VQA benchmarks remain. Revised headline accuracies change the reported evidence without changing these central claims' stated scope.

C2.justification: The interpretation that multigranular alignment benefits medical models remains unchanged. Table 3 rewords the existing warning about classification-based open-answer evaluation and training-test answer overlap, without introducing a distinct limitation or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the documented fine-tuning duration and explicitly attributes the 15-epoch setting to following LLaVA-Med. Data-processing instructions, expert-model lists, prompt templates, and dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work section and bibliography are unchanged. Regrouping existing comparators does not add prior work or revise the dataset and pipeline's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized wording changes in the training-protocol passage and Table 3 caption, together with the updated version stamp. The title, section organization, broader narrative, and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 is reorganized into non-MLLM and MLLM blocks, introduces Ref columns, removes Average columns and asterisk markers, and moves its rewritten caption below the table. Nearby content shifts slightly; all figures and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 3 makes the existing distinction between classification-based reference scores and MLLM results more explicit, modestly improving comparison clarity. Removing average columns reduces convenience, but the component scores remain available. The changed training budget and replacement results do not themselves establish stronger empirical quality; the supported improvement is limited to reporting and presentation.
